html:
Operation Vengeance was the American mission on 18 April 1943 that shot down the plane carrying Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto, the commander of Japan's Combined Fleet and planner of the attack on Pearl Harbor.

American codebreakers, working from the Navy's Station Hypo in Hawaii, read a Japanese message giving Yamamoto's flight plan to inspect troops near Bougainville in the Solomon Islands. Admiral Nimitz approved a plan to intercept him. Sixteen P-38 Lightning fighters flew a long route from Guadalcanal, low over the sea and with radio silence, to meet his bomber and its escort over the island.

They found the planes on time. Yamamoto's bomber crashed in the jungle and he was found dead. Japan lost its best-known commander and was shaken by it. The credit for the kill was later disputed between two of the pilots, Rex Barber and Tom Lanphier.
sum: Operation Vengeance was the American mission on 18 April 1943 that shot down the plane carrying Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto, the commander of Japan's Combined Fleet and planner of the attack on Pearl Harbor.
